conventions: The purity formula הַזָּב and its kin (vv. 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 32, 33): the substantival article takes the supplied he that or him that and heads on the pronoun (rule 41), while the participle takes the whole light-verb rendering hath the issue or hath an issue and heads on the complement issue (rule 44). Where the phrase stands as the nomen rectum of a construct chain, the relational of joins the participle's unit and not the article's, so the article holds only the supplied pronoun: בְשַׂר הַזָּב → the flesh of him that hath the issue (v.7), and likewise vv. 32 and 33, including v.33's הַדָּוָה → of her that is sick. Giving the of to the article's him that unit, which is where it stands, was the competing reading and is named in each unit's note.

נגע בְּ throughout the chapter: the ASV promotes the object to a bare direct object, so the בְּ is unrepresented in every occurrence under rule 40 (vv. 5, 7, 10, 11, 12, 19, 21, 22, 23, 27), and a whosoever or whomsoever fusion standing over the clause does not absorb it — that word carries the quantifier and the relative, not the preposition's relation. The resumptive suffix on such a preposition is likewise unrepresented wherever the ASV writes a plain relative (whomsoever in v.11, which in v.12, whom in v.18) or a bare upon (vv. 9, 20, 22); it enters a unit only inside the whereon fusion of rule 22 (vv. 4, 6, 17, 23, 24, 26).

כֹּל plus an article: before a noun the article is unrepresented, since the ASV writes no the and the every- or any- answers to כֹּל — Every bed (vv. 4, 24, 26), what saddle soever (v.9), everything and anything from כֹּל plus כְּלִי (vv. 4, 26 with the article, v.22 without). Before a substantival participle the article is inside the fusion, because whosoever carries the pronoun rule 41 gives it (vv. 10, 19, 21, 22, 27). Every fusion of this family heads on the quantifier or the noun and never on the relative or the article: כֹּל in whosoever, whatsoever and whomsoever, אִישׁ in v.5's whosoever, and כְּלִי in the article-plus-noun anything of vv. 6 and 23, where no כֹּל stands.

שִׁכְבַת־זָרַע → seed of copulation (vv. 16, 17, 18, 32): the ASV inverts the chain, writing the rectum's English first, so the of stands before the construct noun's own word and belongs to it, headed on copulation, while the rectum זֶרַע keeps the bare seed. This reads which word the of stands before, as rule 29 reads its the and rule 42 its and, rather than applying rule 19's first sentence to a phrase the ASV has turned around. In v.18 the second supplied preposition, with seed, is the adverbial accusative's own under rule 33.

שְׁתֵּי תֹרִים → two turtle doves (vv. 14, 29) heads on doves, not on turtle: the ASV writes doves as the class noun for the bird in the same verse (בְּנֵי יוֹנָה → young pigeons is its counterpart), so turtle is the specifier distinguishing one class word from another under rule 31's tie clause. Heading on turtle was the competing reading and is named in both units.
report: One real cross-verse split, in LEV.15.11. The chapter marks the preposition of נגע בְּ unrepresented under rule 40 in nine places (vv. 5, 7, 10, 12, 19, 21, 22, 23, 27) because the ASV writes a bare object, but v.11 folded that same בְּ, with its resumptive suffix, into the single word whomsoever. Patched: whomsoever now carries כֹּל and the relative only, with בּ and וֹ each their own unrepresented unit — which is how v.12 (which) and v.18 (whom) already read the same relative-plus-resumption shape. This also clears the large-source-unit flag on that unit, from four morphemes to two.

The same patch corrects that unit's source head. v.9's identical כֹּל + אֲשֶׁר fusion (what … soever) heads on the quantifier, as do the five כָל הַ → whosoever units (vv. 10, 19, 21, 22, 27) and v.5's אִישׁ אֲשֶׁר; v.11 alone headed on the relative. It now heads on כֹל, so every fusion of this family in the chapter heads on the quantifier or noun and never on the relative or article.

Checked and found consistent, not split: the whereon fusion (vv. 4, 6, 17, 23, 24, 26) against the bare upon with an unrepresented resumptive (vv. 9, 20, 22), the difference being what the ASV writes; the article under כֹּל (unrepresented before a noun in vv. 4, 9, 24, 26; inside the fusion before a participle); שִׁכְבַת־זָרַע in vv. 16, 17, 18, 32; the הַזָּב formula in vv. 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 32, 33; the sin and burnt offering phrases in vv. 15 and 30; the eighth-day date phrase in vv. 14 and 29; the object marker rendered with in vv. 3, 18, 24 against unrepresented elsewhere; and the apodosis waw (then in vv. 8, 13, 16, 28; unrepresented in vv. 11, 17, 18, 24, where the ASV writes no connective).

The candidate table is blind to added units, so I counted the ASV's connectives against the chapter's waws by hand: every coordinating and in the chapter answers to a written waw except the one in v.19, which is correctly added — the Hebrew sets דָּם יִהְיֶה זֹבָהּ beside the protasis asyndetically. The other added unit, both in v.18, has no counterpart folded into a verb elsewhere; the supplied any of vv. 2, 16, 24 is a determiner joining its noun under rule 15 and is a different case.

BSB: none of the listed disagreements is an error. The R, Td, Sp3ms, To and C groups are the documented convention differences (rules 40, 29, 22, 16, 14), אִישׁ in v.2 is the distributive repetition rendered once under rule 22, and שָׁכֹב in v.24 is rule 56 with no distinct intensifier written. The v.11 patch adds one further R disagreement; that is the rule 40 convention applying uniformly, and no accepted edge was moved to improve the rate.

Promotions: none. The chapter's one candidate — that an inverted construct rendering (שִׁכְבַת־זָרַע → seed of copulation) puts the of on the construct noun it stands before rather than on the rectum, against rule 19's first sentence — is supported by four internally consistent instances here but by no precedent in the tables supplied, and שְׁכָבָה was not among the lemmas queried. Recorded as a convention instead of amending rule 19 on one lemma's evidence.
